correctness.rationale: For each nonempty subset of farthest targets, first-hit probability has Taylor coefficients A=W_d/d! and B=(W_{d+1}-L_d)/(d+1)!, verified from the killed generator and pre-hit holding-time simplex. Inclusion-exclusion and Laplace rescaling yield the N^{-(m+1)/d} term for every fixed m>0, d>=2. An explicit union bound shows nearer targets contribute o(N^{-(m+1)/d}); finite irreducibility controls long tails. Pendant attachment changes only the exit rate at an on-geodesic vertex through order d+1. An independent exact checker passed 6,807 rational assertions and numerical finite-N diagnostics match the two explicit coefficients.

value.rationale: The 2023 cover-time theorem makes leading geodesic locality a central observation. The new formula identifies precisely when off-geodesic rates first matter, proves a strictly positive sensitivity for a natural pendant-branch perturbation, and gives explicit distinct 4/3 versus 5/3 corrections in genuine two-target problems. This structural boundary is meaningful even though the analytical Laplace expansion uses standard tools.
